title: Federal state structure
competency: Explain federalism, how the FDRE Constitution divides power, and its advantages and disadvantages.

keywords.def: A state structure with at least two levels of government, central and regional, with powers divided by a written constitution.

en.text: Federalism has at least two levels of government, central and regional, with powers divided by a written constitution. The federal level handles defence, foreign policy, citizenship and money; regions handle their own constitution, laws, police and development. In Ethiopia, Article 51 lists federal powers and Article 52 regional ones, with residual powers kept by the regions.

screens.ask: Family "Y" has written rules that list the powers of father, mother and children. Is power shared or monopolized?
screens.after: Shared. The written rules act like a constitution dividing power, as in a federal state.
